blocks.title: The shell, the coefficient field and the signature

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The shells in play: the worked Subject shells $\F_{13}$, $\F_{17}$, the coordinate shell $Y=\Fp^{4}$, the coefficient field $K$; the two conjugation registers --- $\It\in\Fp$ Frobenius-fixed, the internal Euclidean phase, and $\w$ the conjugation of the extension; Carrier-scale statements are transfer targets, never sites of computation.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: The class is the datum: $\Fpx/(\Fpx)^{2}$ has order two, any two nonsquares differ by a square factor, and the Lorentzian form depends on $\nu$ only through its class.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The drive is canonical: $g$ is a nonsquare on every shell and the only named residue whose class is nonsquare on every symmetry-complete shell; $\It$, $2$, $2^{-1}$, $-2$ are squares exactly when $\kap$ is even; $e=g^{\It}$ has no stable class; $[g^{-1}]=[g]$. Exhaustive on $\p<2000$.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: The two speed-of-light seats: $\nu=g=c^{2}\cdot(2g)$ exactly on every shell; $[c^{2}]$ is even iff $\kap$ is even, $[2g]$ odd iff $\kap$ is even, the product odd always; the temporal coefficient is not $c^{2}$; anchors $\F_{13}$ ($2^{-1}=7$ nonsquare), $\F_{17}$ ($2,\It,e$ squares), and the laboratory Carrier ($c=171\,106$ base-rational, $1\,204\,281\cdot12=6=g$).
rows.source: Rem.~\ref{rem:nu-not-c}, Cor.~\ref{cor:two-seats}\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08010}{B4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08010}{B4}, \leanwit{FrcLedger}{p08010}{B4} \lean{Dirac.nu\_factorisation, Dirac.two\_g\_class, Dirac.named\_residues, Dirac.shell13, Dirac.carrier\_constants, FRC.Dirac.nu\_factorisation, FRC.Dirac.carrier\_constants}

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: The square class is chronon parity: the squares are $\langle g^{2}\rangle$, a residue's class is the parity of its drive-step count; on $\kap$-even shells every element of $Q_4=\{1,\It,-1,-\It\}$ is a square, so the order-four chart grading carries no signature. Exhaustive over every primitive root of $\F_{13}$, $\F_{17}$; Euler form on $\p<2000$.

rows.label: B6
rows.predicate: Norm growth and parity: $N(gz)=g^{2}N(z)$ with $g^{2}$ a square, the single-chronon multiplier $g$ odd, $x^{2}=\nu$ unsolvable in $\Fp$; the flip $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ preserves the parity class.

rows.label: B7
rows.predicate: Signature lives on $\Fp$: the Euclidean form has $\p^{3}+\p^{2}-\p$ zeros (hyperbolic, Witt index two), $Q_\nu$ has $\p^{3}-\p^{2}+\p$ (elliptic, Witt index one) on every symmetry-complete $\p<60$; $2353$ and $2041$ at $\p=13$; over $K$ every element of $\Fp$ is a square and the dichotomy collapses.

rows.label: B8
rows.predicate: One-way and two-way transport: comparison (two-way) readings are even-parity, the one-way single-chronon multiplier odd, and the null-cone slope $\sqrt\nu=g^{1/2}$ is no base-field ratio --- light-like transport carries no registered velocity, only its square class. Falsifier: a registered one-way velocity, or a two-way constant that changes under the synchronisation gauge $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ (B6).

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The Hermitian form $\langle\psi,\phi\rangle_X=\sum\overline{\psi(x)}\phi(x)$ on $\calH(X)$, the adjoint, the finite unitary group; the Euclidean configuration space $X_d=\Fp^{d}$ with translations $T_u$, forward and backward differences and the Laplacian $\Delta_E$; the Hamiltonian $H_{E,V,\vkap}=-\vkap\Delta_E+M_V$ with the stiffness $\vkap$ distinct from the capacity $\kap$.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: The form is Hermitian and nondegenerate; $T_u$ is unitary with $T_u^{\dagger}=T_{-u}$; $\Delta_E$ and $H_{E,V,\vkap}$ are self-adjoint; under $A\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\Fp)$ the pullback $A_*$ intertwines translations, differences and Laplacians of the two frames.

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: The Cayley step $U_{\alpha,H}=(I-\alpha H)^{-1}(I+\alpha H)$ for $\alpha\in K^{-}$ (the recursion $(I-\alpha H)\psi_{n+1}=(I+\alpha H)\psi_n$); the admissible set $\calA(H)=\{\alpha\in K^{-}:\det(I-\alpha H)\ne0\}$.

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Exact Hermitian preservation: for self-adjoint $H$ and admissible $\alpha$ the Cayley step is unitary, and every orbit is periodic.

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: The finite Cayley transform: $\varphi(\lambda)=(1+\alpha\lambda)/(1-\alpha\lambda)$ is defined on all of $\Fp$, takes values in the norm-one torus $N^{1}$, and with $\varphi(\infty)=-1$ bijects $\mathbb P^{1}(\Fp)$ onto $N^{1}$, $|N^{1}|=\p+1$; the unitary group of one channel is $N^{1}$; the orientation gauge $\alpha\mapsto-\alpha$ inverts every $\varphi(\lambda)$ and imports the derived orientation of the shell.

rows.label: C6
rows.predicate: The $\F_{13}$ Schr\"odinger example: $H=-\Delta_E$ on $\F_{13}$ is nilpotent, so $\calA(H)=K^{-}$; at $\alpha=c$, $U^{13}=I$; every $\alpha=kc$, $k\ne0$, gives order $13$, and $U$ is unitary for the form.

A2.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.field
A2.doc: 8:A2 — the field structure under `¬ IsSquare ν`, `z⁻¹ = z̄/N(z)` (a `def`, not an instance: the hypothesis is not a class).

A2.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.exists_boost_eq
A2.doc: 8:D5, 8:A2 — Hilbert 90 on the torus: every `u ∈ N¹` is a boost — `u = (1 + u)/(1 + ū)` for `u ≠ −1`, and `−1 = w/w̄`.

A2.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.mul_conj
A2.doc: 8:A2 — the norm is the product with the conjugate: `z z̄ = N(z)`, a base-field element.

A5.name: FRC.Dirac.carrier_constants
A5.doc: 8:B4, 8:A5 [value] — the laboratory Carrier `Ω = 2 408 561`: `c = 171 106` is base-rational with `c² = 2⁻¹` (`171106² · 2 ≡ 1`), `2⁻¹ = 1 204 281`, and the two seats compose: `2⁻¹ · 12 ≡ 6 = g`.

A5.name: FRC.Dirac.minimal_admissible
A5.doc: 8:D12, 8:A5 [value] — `𝔽₁₇` (`κ = 4`) is the minimal admissible shell: `17 ≡ 5 (mod 12)`, and no capacity below `4` is admissible (`κ = 1, 3` odd, `κ = 2` gives `9`).

A5.name: FRC.Dirac.carrier_constants
A5.doc: 8:B4, 8:A5 [value] — the laboratory Carrier `Ω = 2 408 561`: `c = 171 106` is base-rational with `c² = 2⁻¹ = 1 204 281`, and the two factors compose, `2⁻¹ · (2g) = 1 204 281 · 12 = 6 = g`.

B2.name: FRC.Dirac.class_datum
B2.doc: 8:B2 — two nonsquares differ by a square factor: `F^×/(F^×)²` has order two (Lemma `class-datum`); the Lorentzian form then depends on `ν` only through its class, `−(m²ν) x₀² = −ν (m x₀)²`.

B2.name: FRC.Dirac.form_class
B2.doc: 8:B2 — the rescaling `x₀ ↦ m x₀` identifies the forms of `ν` and `m²ν`: a ring identity, the content of the clause "the form depends on `ν` only through its class".

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_nonsquare
B3.doc: 8:B3 — the drive is a nonsquare (`g^{(p−1)/2} = −1`), and so is its inverse `g^{p−2}`: `[g⁻¹] = [g]`.

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.named_residues
B3.doc: 8:B3, 8:B4 — on the shell `p = 4κ + 1`: `2` is a square ⟺ `κ` even (the second supplementary law), and so `2⁻¹ = c²` and `−2` (`−1` a square); the quarter-turn `i = g^{−κ} = g^{3κ}` is a square ⟺ `κ` even.

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.shell13
B3.doc: 8:D12, 8:B4, 8:B3 [value] — `𝔽₁₃` with `ν = g = 2`, `x = y = 1`: `A = 10`, `B = 2`, `A² − νB² = 1`; `2⁻¹ = 7` is a nonsquare and `e = 2^5 = 6` a nonsquare; `2` is primitive (`orderOf 2 = 12`).

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.shell17
B3.doc: 8:D12, 8:B3 [value] — `𝔽₁₇` (`κ = 4`) with `ν = g = 3`, `i = 4`: `A = 15`, `B = 1`, `A² − νB² = 1`; `2 = 6²`, `i = 2²`, `e = 3⁴ = 13 = 8²` are squares (so the class of `e` is not stable across shells), `3` a nonsquare, `3` primitive; `17 ≡ 5 (mod 12)`, and no capacity below `4` is even and `≡ 1 (mod 3)`: the minimal admissible shell.

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_nonsquare
B3.doc: 8:B3 — the drive is a nonsquare on every frame (`m = 1`).

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.inv_drive_nonsquare
B3.doc: 8:B3, 8:B6 — the reframing flip preserves the class: the inverse of the drive is a nonsquare (an odd power of `g`), so `[g⁻¹] = [g]`.

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.quarter_class
B3.doc: 8:B3 — `i` is a square exactly when the capacity is even (the eighth root of unity exists iff `8 ∣ p − 1`).

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.two_class
B3.doc: 8:B3 — `2`, `2⁻¹` and `−2` are squares exactly when the capacity is even (the second supplementary law at tier 0, 14-entropy's `two_is_square_iff`, and `−1 = (g^κ)²`).

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.anchors
B3.doc: 8:B4, 8:B3, 8:D12 [value] — the anchors: on `𝔽₁₃` (`g = 2`, `i = 5`) `2⁻¹ = 7` is a nonsquare and `e = g^i = 6` is a nonsquare; on `𝔽₁₇` (`g = 3`, `i = 4`) `2 = 6²`, `i = 2²` and `e = 3⁴ = 13 = 8²` are squares, and `ν = g = 3` is the only nonsquare among the named residues — so the class of `e` is not stable across shells (B3).

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.nu_factorisation
B4.doc: 8:B4 — with `c² = 2⁻¹`, the temporal coefficient factors identically, `ν = g = c² · (2g)`, on every shell (Corollary `two-seats`; the classes of the two factors: `named_residues`, `two_g_class`).

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.two_g_class
B4.doc: 8:B4 — the cofactor's class: for a primitive root `g` (a nonsquare), `2g` is a square exactly when `2` is not, i.e. exactly when `κ` is odd on the shell `p = 4κ + 1` (`named_residues`): the product `ν = g` is odd always, `c² = 2⁻¹` even exactly on the admissibility class.

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.named_residues
B4.doc: 8:B3, 8:B4 — on the shell `p = 4κ + 1`: `2` is a square ⟺ `κ` even (the second supplementary law), and so `2⁻¹ = c²` and `−2` (`−1` a square); the quarter-turn `i = g^{−κ} = g^{3κ}` is a square ⟺ `κ` even.

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.shell13
B4.doc: 8:D12, 8:B4, 8:B3 [value] — `𝔽₁₃` with `ν = g = 2`, `x = y = 1`: `A = 10`, `B = 2`, `A² − νB² = 1`; `2⁻¹ = 7` is a nonsquare and `e = 2^5 = 6` a nonsquare; `2` is primitive (`orderOf 2 = 12`).

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.carrier_constants
B4.doc: 8:B4, 8:A5 [value] — the laboratory Carrier `Ω = 2 408 561`: `c = 171 106` is base-rational with `c² = 2⁻¹` (`171106² · 2 ≡ 1`), `2⁻¹ = 1 204 281`, and the two seats compose: `2⁻¹ · 12 ≡ 6 = g`.

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.nu_factorisation
B4.doc: 8:B4 — the factorisation of the coefficient: with `c² = 2⁻¹`, `ν = g = c²·(2g)` exactly on every shell, and the cofactor `2g` is a square exactly when `κ` is odd — the product `g` odd always (Corollary `two-seats`).

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.carrier_constants
B4.doc: 8:B4, 8:A5 [value] — the laboratory Carrier `Ω = 2 408 561`: `c = 171 106` is base-rational with `c² = 2⁻¹ = 1 204 281`, and the two factors compose, `2⁻¹ · (2g) = 1 204 281 · 12 = 6 = g`.

B5.name: FRC.Dirac.parity_iff
B5.doc: 8:B5 — the square class is chronon parity: for a primitive root `g` (`orderOf g = p − 1`), `g^k` is a square exactly when `k` is even (Theorem `parity`).

B5.name: FRC.Dirac.parity_iff
B5.doc: 8:B5 — the square class is chronon parity: on every frame, `g^m` is a square exactly when the drive-step count `m` is even (Theorem `parity`).

B6.name: FRC.Dirac.norm_growth
B6.doc: 8:B6 — norm growth: `N(gz) = g² N(z)` (Theorem `even-transport`; `g²` is even by `parity_iff`).

B6.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.norm_scale
B6.doc: 8:B6 — norm growth: `N(c z) = c² N(z)` for every base residue `c`; one chronon of drive multiplies every norm by `g²`, a square.

B6.name: FRC.Dirac.inv_drive_nonsquare
B6.doc: 8:B3, 8:B6 — the reframing flip preserves the class: the inverse of the drive is a nonsquare (an odd power of `g`), so `[g⁻¹] = [g]`.

B7.name: FRC.Dirac.ext_square
B7.doc: 8:B7 — over the quadratic extension every element of `F_p` is a square: a nonsquare `a = m² ν` becomes `(m w)²`, so the Euclidean–Lorentzian dichotomy collapses in `K` (Remark `signature-record`).

B7.name: FRC.Dirac.zeros5
B7.doc: 8:B7 [value] — on `𝔽₅` the Euclidean form has `5³ + 5² − 5 = 145` zeros and the Lorentzian form (`ν = g = 2`) has `5³ − 5² + 5 = 105`: the hyperbolic and the elliptic form part on the base shell.

C2.name: FRC.Dirac.herm_star
C2.doc: 8:C2 — Hermitian symmetry `⟨ψ, φ⟩* = ⟨φ, ψ⟩`; linearity in the second slot, conjugate-linearity in the first.

C2.name: FRC.Dirac.herm_nondegenerate
C2.doc: 8:C2 — nondegeneracy: `⟨ψ, φ⟩ = 0` for every `φ` forces `ψ = 0` (Lemma `hermitian-nondeg`; the test function is the point mass at `x₀`).

C2.name: FRC.Dirac.herm_translate
C2.doc: 8:C2 — every translation is unitary for the form, and `T_u† = T_{−u}` (Proposition `translation-unitary`).

C2.name: FRC.Dirac.herm_translate_adjoint
C2.doc: 8:C2 — the adjoint of a translation is the opposite translation, `T_u† = T_{−u}` (Proposition `translation-unitary`).

C2.name: FRC.Dirac.herm_laplacian
C2.doc: 8:C2 — the Laplacian along one direction is self-adjoint, `⟨Δψ, φ⟩ = ⟨ψ, Δφ⟩` (Proposition `laplacian-sa`; the `d`-dimensional Laplacian is the sum over the directions), and with it every Hamiltonian `−ϰΔ + M_V` with `ϰ` and `V` Frobenius-fixed (Corollary `hamiltonian-sa`).

C2.name: FRC.Dirac.herm_hamiltonian
C2.doc: 8:C2 — every Hamiltonian `−ϰΔ + M_V` with `ϰ` and `V` Frobenius-fixed is self-adjoint (Corollary `hamiltonian-sa`).

C4.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley_unitary
C4.doc: 8:C4, 8:D10 — the exact Hermitian preservation, for any anti-involution `σ` of the operator ring (the adjoint of a nondegenerate Hermitian form, or the `X`-adjoint of the spinor form): if `σ h = h`, the scalar `a` is central with `σ a = −a`, and `1 − a h` is a unit, then `u = (1 − a h)⁻¹ (1 + a h)` satisfies `σ u · u = 1` — the Cayley step is unitary (Theorem `cayley-preservation`). For D10 the premise `σ h = h` is the `X`-self-adjointness of `𝒟^s − m` (D9's operator clause, decided by the package at `p = 5, 13, 17` and not proved here).

C4.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley_periodic
C4.doc: 8:C4 — every orbit is periodic: a unit of a finite ring has finite order (Corollary `finite-periodicity`).

C5.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.cayley_norm
C5.doc: 8:C5 — the Cayley transform takes values in the norm-one torus: `N(φ_α(λ)) = 1` for every `λ ∈ F`, the denominator never vanishing (Theorem `cayley-transform`).

C5.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.cayley_injective
C5.doc: 8:C5 — `φ_α(λ) = (1 + αλ)/(1 − αλ)`, `α = kw ≠ 0`, is injective on `F` (a nonconstant Möbius map): the self-adjoint line embeds in the torus (Theorem `cayley-transform`).

C5.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.cayley_gauge
C5.doc: 8:C5 — the orientation gauge `α ↦ −α` inverts every value: `φ_{−α}(λ) · φ_α(λ) = 1` (Remark `forward-step`: the forward step imports the derived orientation of the shell).

C5.name: FRC.Dirac.torus_counts
C5.doc: 8:D5, 8:D12, 8:C5, 8:F2 [value] — the boost torus: `|N¹| = 14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` (`ν = 2`) and `18` on `𝔽₁₇` (`ν = 3`); the unit-norm circle of the chart has `p − 1` points: `12` and `16` (8:F2).

C6.name: FRC.Dirac.kinetic_nilpotent
C6.doc: 8:E4 (1), 8:C6 — `h = c (t + t^{p−1} − 2) = c t^{p−1} (t − 1)²` and with it `a h` for any `a` commuting with `t` and `c` is nilpotent, `(a h)^p = 0`, so `1 − a h` is a unit: the Cayley step is defined for every `a` — `𝒜(H) = K⁻` (Corollary `kinetic-admissible`; `H = −Δ` at `c = −1`).

C6.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley_period
C6.doc: 8:E4 (1), 8:C6 — the period: for a nilpotent `n` with `n^p = 0` and `2` a unit, the Cayley step `u = (1 − n)⁻¹(1 + n)` is unipotent — `u − 1 = 2(1 − n)⁻¹ n`, `(u − 1)^p = 0`, `u^p = 1` — and `u ≠ 1` when `n ≠ 0`, so in the prime characteristic `ord(U) = p` exactly (Theorem `period-dichotomy` (1); on `𝔽₁₃`, `ord(U_{kw, −Δ}) = 13` for every `k ≠ 0`, Example `cayley-13`).

C6.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley13_values
C6.doc: 8:C6, 8:E4 [value] — the Cayley step of `H = −Δ` on `𝔽₁₃` has order exactly `13` at `α = w` and at `α = c = 6w` (`c² = 7 = 2⁻¹`).

D2.name: FRC.Dirac.clifford
D2.doc: 8:D2 — the Clifford relations `γ^μ γ^ν + γ^ν γ^μ = 2 η_{μν} I₄`, `η = diag(−ν, 1, 1, 1)`, from `i² = −1` and `w² = ν` alone (Proposition `clifford`), by the block computation of its proof: `β² = I`, `(ρ^k)² = −I`, `ρ^jρ^k + ρ^kρ^j = 0`, `βρ^k + ρ^kβ = 0`.

D2.name: FRC.Dirac.pauli
D2.doc: 8:D2 — the Pauli identities `σ^j σ^k + σ^k σ^j = 2 δ_{jk} I₂` over `K`, from `i² = −1`.

D2.name: FRC.Dirac.clifford_values
D2.doc: 8:D2 [value] — the Clifford relations hold on `𝔽₁₃` (`ν = 2`, `i = 5`), `𝔽₁₇` (`ν = 3`, `i = 4`) and `𝔽₅` (`ν = 2`, `i = 2`).

D5.name: FRC.Dirac.boost_entries
D5.doc: 8:D5, 8:D7 — `Λ(x, y) ∈ O(Q_ν)`: `A² − νB² = 1` (Proposition `boost-orthogonal`); and the group law `Λ(x, y)Λ(u, v) = Λ(xu + νyv, xv + yu)` on the entries, with `Λ(1, 0) = I` and `Λ(x, −y) = Λ(x, y)⁻¹` (Proposition `boost-subgroup`).

D5.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.boost_mem
D5.doc: 8:D5 — the boost of every unit lies in `N¹`: `N(z/z̄) = 1`.

D5.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.boost_eq_one_iff
D5.doc: 8:D5 — the kernel of the boost is the scalar line: `z/z̄ = 1 ⟺ z̄ = z ⟺ z ∈ F`.

D5.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.boost_range
D5.doc: 8:D5 — the range of the boost is exactly `N¹` (Lemma `boost-torus`: `G_ν ≅ K^×/F^× ≅ N¹`).

D5.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.normOne_cyclic
D5.doc: 8:D5, 8:C5 — `N¹` is cyclic (a finite subgroup of the units of a field), of order `p + 1` on `F = 𝔽_p`: `N¹ ≅ C_{p+1}`.

D5.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.order_three_iff
D5.doc: 8:D5 — the triality clause: the torus carries an element of order three exactly when `3 ∣ p + 1` (Cauchy in the cyclic group `C_{p+1}`; `|G_3| = 18` at `17`, `|G_2| = 14` at `13`).

D5.name: FRC.Dirac.torus_counts
D5.doc: 8:D5, 8:D12, 8:C5, 8:F2 [value] — the boost torus: `|N¹| = 14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` (`ν = 2`) and `18` on `𝔽₁₇` (`ν = 3`); the unit-norm circle of the chart has `p − 1` points: `12` and `16` (8:F2).

D5.name: FRC.Dirac.triality_values
D5.doc: 8:D5 [value] — an element of order three on the torus of `𝔽₁₇`, none on the torus of `𝔽₁₃`.

D6.name: FRC.Dirac.spin_conjugation
D6.doc: 8:D6, 8:D7 (the transported gammas) — spin conjugation up to the scalar `δ`: `M² = ν`, `(x − yM) γ⁰ (x + yM) = (x² + νy²) γ⁰ − 2xyν γ¹`, `(x − yM) γ¹ (x + yM) = −2xy γ⁰ + (x² + νy²) γ¹`, and `M` commutes with `γ²` and `γ³` (Proposition `spin-conjugation`; the division by `δ = x² − νy²` onto `A = (x² + νy²)/δ`, `B = −2xy/δ` is `spin_conjugation_AB`); `y ↦ −y` gives the transported gammas `γ̂⁰ = Aγ⁰ − νBγ¹`, `γ̂¹ = −Bγ⁰ + Aγ¹` (Proposition `transported-dirac-form`, the pullback identity and the transported factorization not formalised).

D6.name: FRC.Dirac.spin_conjugation_AB
D6.doc: 8:D6 — the spin conjugation with the inverse: for `δ = x² − νy² ≠ 0`, `S⁻¹ = δ⁻¹(x − yM)` and `S⁻¹γ⁰S = Aγ⁰ + νBγ¹`, `S⁻¹γ¹S = Bγ⁰ + Aγ¹` with `A = (x² + νy²)/δ`, `B = −2xy/δ` (Proposition `spin-conjugation`).

D7.name: FRC.Dirac.spin_conjugation
D7.doc: 8:D6, 8:D7 (the transported gammas) — spin conjugation up to the scalar `δ`: `M² = ν`, `(x − yM) γ⁰ (x + yM) = (x² + νy²) γ⁰ − 2xyν γ¹`, `(x − yM) γ¹ (x + yM) = −2xy γ⁰ + (x² + νy²) γ¹`, and `M` commutes with `γ²` and `γ³` (Proposition `spin-conjugation`; the division by `δ = x² − νy²` onto `A = (x² + νy²)/δ`, `B = −2xy/δ` is `spin_conjugation_AB`); `y ↦ −y` gives the transported gammas `γ̂⁰ = Aγ⁰ − νBγ¹`, `γ̂¹ = −Bγ⁰ + Aγ¹` (Proposition `transported-dirac-form`, the pullback identity and the transported factorization not formalised).

D7.name: FRC.Dirac.boost_entries
D7.doc: 8:D5, 8:D7 — `Λ(x, y) ∈ O(Q_ν)`: `A² − νB² = 1` (Proposition `boost-orthogonal`); and the group law `Λ(x, y)Λ(u, v) = Λ(xu + νyv, xv + yu)` on the entries, with `Λ(1, 0) = I` and `Λ(x, −y) = Λ(x, y)⁻¹` (Proposition `boost-subgroup`).

D9.name: FRC.Dirac.spinor_twist
D9.doc: 8:D9 — the spinor twist: `X² = ν`, `X` commutes with `γ⁰, γ¹, γ³` and anticommutes with `γ²` (Lemma `spinor-form`, the algebraic part).

D9.name: FRC.Dirac.gamma_dagger
D9.doc: 8:D9 — under the conjugate transpose (Frobenius fixing `i`, negating `w`): `(γ⁰)† = −γ⁰`, `(γ¹)† = −γ¹`, `(γ²)† = +γ²` (the obstruction: `σ²` is antisymmetric with `i` Frobenius-fixed), `(γ³)† = −γ³`, and `X† = X` for the twist `X = γ⁰γ¹γ³` (Lemma `spinor-form`).

D9.name: FRC.Dirac.twist_adjoint
D9.doc: 8:D9 — the twist conjugates every gamma to its negative, `(γ^μ)† X = −X γ^μ` (so `X⁻¹(γ^μ)†X = −γ^μ`), while the `γ⁰`-twist leaves mixed signs: `(γ⁰)† γ⁰ = −γ⁰γ⁰` but `(γ¹)† γ⁰ = +γ⁰γ¹` (Lemma `spinor-form`).

D10.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley_unitary
D10.doc: 8:C4, 8:D10 — the exact Hermitian preservation, for any anti-involution `σ` of the operator ring (the adjoint of a nondegenerate Hermitian form, or the `X`-adjoint of the spinor form): if `σ h = h`, the scalar `a` is central with `σ a = −a`, and `1 − a h` is a unit, then `u = (1 − a h)⁻¹ (1 + a h)` satisfies `σ u · u = 1` — the Cayley step is unitary (Theorem `cayley-preservation`). For D10 the premise `σ h = h` is the `X`-self-adjointness of `𝒟^s − m` (D9's operator clause, decided by the package at `p = 5, 13, 17` and not proved here).

D10.name: FRC.Dirac.translation_nilpotent
D10.doc: 8:E4 (1), 8:C6, 8:D10 — the translation `t` of order `p` (`t^p = 1`) has `(t − 1)^p = 0` in characteristic `p`: the kinetic Hamiltonians and the symmetric differences are nilpotent (Theorem `period-dichotomy` (1), Corollary `kinetic-admissible`).

D11.name: FRC.Dirac.lift_adjoint
D11.doc: 8:D11 — the lift's adjoint: `S† = S(x, −y)` for Frobenius-fixed `x, y` (so, `X` commuting with `M`, `S^# = X⁻¹S†X = S(x, −y)`), and `S(x, −y) S(x, y) = (x² − νy²) I = δ I` (Proposition `two-diracs`).

D11.name: FRC.Dirac.lift_transport
D11.doc: 8:D11 — the transport of the spinor form: for a lift `S = x + yM` with Frobenius-fixed `x, y`, `S† X S = (x² − νy²) X = δ X` — norm-one lifts preserve the form exactly, and the odd coset scales it by the lift norm `δ` (Proposition `two-diracs`).

D12.name: FRC.Dirac.shell13
D12.doc: 8:D12, 8:B4, 8:B3 [value] — `𝔽₁₃` with `ν = g = 2`, `x = y = 1`: `A = 10`, `B = 2`, `A² − νB² = 1`; `2⁻¹ = 7` is a nonsquare and `e = 2^5 = 6` a nonsquare; `2` is primitive (`orderOf 2 = 12`).

D12.name: FRC.Dirac.shell17
D12.doc: 8:D12, 8:B3 [value] — `𝔽₁₇` (`κ = 4`) with `ν = g = 3`, `i = 4`: `A = 15`, `B = 1`, `A² − νB² = 1`; `2 = 6²`, `i = 2²`, `e = 3⁴ = 13 = 8²` are squares (so the class of `e` is not stable across shells), `3` a nonsquare, `3` primitive; `17 ≡ 5 (mod 12)`, and no capacity below `4` is even and `≡ 1 (mod 3)`: the minimal admissible shell.

D12.name: FRC.Dirac.torus_counts
D12.doc: 8:D5, 8:D12, 8:C5, 8:F2 [value] — the boost torus: `|N¹| = 14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` (`ν = 2`) and `18` on `𝔽₁₇` (`ν = 3`); the unit-norm circle of the chart has `p − 1` points: `12` and `16` (8:F2).

D12.name: FRC.Dirac.anchors
D12.doc: 8:B4, 8:B3, 8:D12 [value] — the anchors: on `𝔽₁₃` (`g = 2`, `i = 5`) `2⁻¹ = 7` is a nonsquare and `e = g^i = 6` is a nonsquare; on `𝔽₁₇` (`g = 3`, `i = 4`) `2 = 6²`, `i = 2²` and `e = 3⁴ = 13 = 8²` are squares, and `ν = g = 3` is the only nonsquare among the named residues — so the class of `e` is not stable across shells (B3).

D12.name: FRC.Dirac.minimal_admissible
D12.doc: 8:D12, 8:A5 [value] — `𝔽₁₇` (`κ = 4`) is the minimal admissible shell: `17 ≡ 5 (mod 12)`, and no capacity below `4` is admissible (`κ = 1, 3` odd, `κ = 2` gives `9`).

E2.name: FRC.Dirac.loss_factor_one
E2.doc: 8:E2 — a self-map of a finite set is bijective exactly when its image count is the whole count (loss factor `1`): `|f(X)| = |X| ⟺ f bijective` (Proposition `loss-factor-one`).

E2.name: FRC.Dirac.power_map_count
E2.doc: 8:E2 — the power-map count on the phase cycle: `x ↦ x^ε` on `(ZMod p)ˣ` has image of size `(p − 1)/gcd(ε, p − 1)`, and its kernel — the fibre over `1`, of which every nonempty fibre is a coset — has `gcd(ε, p − 1)` elements (Proposition `power-map-count`, on the cyclic group of order `p − 1`).

E2.name: FRC.Dirac.power_map13
E2.doc: 8:E2 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃`: the images of `x ↦ x^ε` have `(p − 1)/gcd(ε, 12)` elements — `12, 6, 4, 3, 2, 1` for `ε = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12` (loss factors `1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12`).

E3.name: FRC.Dirac.unit_loss_factor_one
E3.doc: 8:E3 — an invertible map has loss factor one: left multiplication by a unit is a bijection (the Cayley propagators and the boost transports).

E4.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley_period
E4.doc: 8:E4 (1), 8:C6 — the period: for a nilpotent `n` with `n^p = 0` and `2` a unit, the Cayley step `u = (1 − n)⁻¹(1 + n)` is unipotent — `u − 1 = 2(1 − n)⁻¹ n`, `(u − 1)^p = 0`, `u^p = 1` — and `u ≠ 1` when `n ≠ 0`, so in the prime characteristic `ord(U) = p` exactly (Theorem `period-dichotomy` (1); on `𝔽₁₃`, `ord(U_{kw, −Δ}) = 13` for every `k ≠ 0`, Example `cayley-13`).

E4.name: FRC.Dirac.kinetic_nilpotent
E4.doc: 8:E4 (1), 8:C6 — `h = c (t + t^{p−1} − 2) = c t^{p−1} (t − 1)²` and with it `a h` for any `a` commuting with `t` and `c` is nilpotent, `(a h)^p = 0`, so `1 − a h` is a unit: the Cayley step is defined for every `a` — `𝒜(H) = K⁻` (Corollary `kinetic-admissible`; `H = −Δ` at `c = −1`).

E4.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.torus_period
E4.doc: 8:E4 (2) — every phase on the torus has `u^{p+1} = 1`: a potential propagator, diagonal with entries in `N¹`, has order dividing `p + 1`; and some phase has order exactly `p + 1` (the torus is cyclic), so the bound is attained (Theorem `period-dichotomy` (2)).

E4.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley13_values
E4.doc: 8:C6, 8:E4 [value] — the Cayley step of `H = −Δ` on `𝔽₁₃` has order exactly `13` at `α = w` and at `α = c = 6w` (`c² = 7 = 2⁻¹`).

E4.name: FRC.Dirac.potential_orders
E4.doc: 8:E4 [value] — the potential propagator of `V = id` has order `14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` and `18` on `𝔽₁₇`, the least common multiple of the phase orders, every phase of norm one.

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.latitude_identities
F2.doc: 8:F2 — on the shell `p = 4κ + 1`: `4κ = −1`, so `κ = −4⁻¹`, the energy radius `1 + κ = 3·4⁻¹`, `π = 2κ = −2⁻¹`; `g^κ = −i` for `i = g^{−κ} = g^{3κ}` (`−1 = g^{2κ}`); and `κ + 1`, the first rung past the midpoint of the ladder `1, …, 2κ`, is still a rung.

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.ladder
F2.doc: 8:F2 — the ladder `1, …, 2κ`: `κ + 1`, the first rung past the midpoint `κ`, is still a rung.

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.four_kappa
F2.doc: 8:F2 — `4κ ≡ −1` on the shell (`4κ = p − 1`), so `κ = −4⁻¹` and the energy radius `1 + κ = 3·4⁻¹`.

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.terminal_latitude
F2.doc: 8:F2 — the terminal latitude: `π = 2κ = −2⁻¹` (`= −c²`); the quarter-cycle shift `m ↦ m + κ` on the ladder is multiplication by `g^κ = −i` (`quarterTurn_eq_pow`, `i = −g^κ` by definition).

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.torus_counts
F2.doc: 8:D5, 8:D12, 8:C5, 8:F2 [value] — the boost torus: `|N¹| = 14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` (`ν = 2`) and `18` on `𝔽₁₇` (`ν = 3`); the unit-norm circle of the chart has `p − 1` points: `12` and `16` (8:F2).

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_chi
F3.doc: 8:F3 (2) — the characters are eigenvectors of the drive with eigenvalue `g^{−k}`: the winding-`k` mode acquires the phase `g^{−k}` per chronon (Theorem `zonal`).

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_sum
F3.doc: 8:F3 (1) — the drive is a permutation of the cycle: it preserves the sum defining the form (unitary).

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.chi_isotropy
F3.doc: 8:F3 (3) — isotropy: the character values are Frobenius-fixed, so `⟨χ_k, χ_k⟩ = Σ_x x^{2k}`, which is `0` unless `(p − 1) ∣ 2k` and `−1` otherwise (Mathlib's `FiniteField.sum_pow_units`): every character line is isotropic except `k = 0` and `k = (p − 1)/2`.

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.exceptional_eigen
F3.doc: 8:F3 (3), 8:F4 — the exceptional eigenvalues are `±1`: on the shell `p = 4κ + 1` with `g` of order `4κ`, `k = 2κ` gives `g^{−2κ} = −1` (and `k = 0` gives `1`); and these are all of `N¹ ∩ 𝔽_p`: a base-field element of norm one (`u ū = u² = 1`) is `±1` (Corollary `sectors`).

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_eigen
F3.doc: 8:F3 — the drive pullback on the characters: with `y = g⁻¹`, `χ_k(g^{j}) = y^k · χ_k(g^{j+1})` for every `j, k` — the winding-`k` mode acquires the phase `g^{−k}` per chronon (Theorem `zonal` (2)).

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.exceptional_eigen
F3.doc: 8:F3 — the exceptional eigenvalue: `k = 2κ` gives `g^{−2κ} = −1` (and `k = 0` gives `1`) — the intersection `N¹ ∩ μ_{p−1} = {±1}` of the norm-one torus with the phase cycle.

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.isotropy
F3.doc: 8:F3 — isotropy: the character line `χ_k` is isotropic, `Σ_j χ_k(g^j)² = Σ_j g^{2jk} = 0`, unless `(p − 1) ∣ 2k`; on the two exceptional lines the sum is `p − 1 = −1 ≠ 0` (Theorem `zonal` (3)).

F4.name: FRC.Dirac.sector_separation
F4.doc: 8:F4 — the sector separation: `ord(g⁻¹) = ord(g) = p − 1`, the drive's phases run on the split cycle `μ_{p−1}`, while the norm-one torus has order `p + 1`; and there are no meridional plane waves: no `K`-valued character of the translation cycle `C_p`, since `p ∤ p² − 1` — no unit of `K` has order `p` (`gcd(p, |Kˣ|) = 1`).

F4.name: FRC.Dirac.dispersion
F4.doc: 8:F4 — the dispersion relation on the cycle: `−Δ_Φ χ_k = (2 − g^k − g^{−k}) χ_k` with `Δ_Φ = D + D⁻¹ − 2` (the finite band curve).

F4.name: FRC.Dirac.exceptional_eigen
F4.doc: 8:F3 (3), 8:F4 — the exceptional eigenvalues are `±1`: on the shell `p = 4κ + 1` with `g` of order `4κ`, `k = 2κ` gives `g^{−2κ} = −1` (and `k = 0` gives `1`); and these are all of `N¹ ∩ 𝔽_p`: a base-field element of norm one (`u ū = u² = 1`) is `±1` (Corollary `sectors`).

F4.name: FRC.Dirac.sector_separation
F4.doc: 8:F4 — sector separation: the inverse of the drive is primitive of order `p − 1` (`ord(g⁻¹) = p − 1`, so the free evolution is no Cayley step, whose scalar phases have order dividing `p + 1`), and the norm-one torus meets the base field in `{±1}` alone (`u² = 1 ⇒ u = ±1`).
